title: ctDNA support vector machine predicts immunotherapy benefit in advanced NSCLC
summary: An SVM trained on 41 LASSO-selected somatic mutations from baseline ctDNA exome data in the OAK trial (n=303) predicted durable clinical benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors, with AUC 0.87 in OAK, 0.92 in the independent POPLAR cohort (n=97) and 0.83 in a regional multicenter cohort (n=41). It also stratified survival by SVM score. The data are retrospective trial data and validation cohorts are small.
ai_technology: Support vector machine on 41 LASSO-selected somatic mutations from pretreatment ctDNA whole-exome sequencing

evidence.tested: Independent validation in the POPLAR trial cohort (n=97) and a regional multicenter cohort (n=41); retrospective.
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation, larger cohorts and effect on treatment choice; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learns a mutation-based score predicting immunotherapy benefit.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
